The culture after 5 days showed radiated powdery colonies of khaki yellow color (Figure 1). Direct examination of the colony showed terminal and intercalary chlamydospores (Figure 2).

report.source_text: Faced with the difficulty of morphological identification, a real-time PCR was performed using the DermaGenius® 2.0 kit (PathoNostics, the Netherlands). Data analysis was performed using the 2nd-derivative and Tm-calling function of the LC480 software (version 1.5.1.62 SP2). This allowed the identification of Epidermophyton floccosum (Figure 3).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 70-year-old diabetic patient on tocilizumab presented with fever and a painful erythematous, well-demarcated, warm, tender plaque on the right leg accompanied by scaly plantar keratoderma and intertrigo of toe web spaces. Direct mycological examination revealed mycelial filaments, and culture showed characteristic radiated powdery khaki yellow colonies with terminal and intercalary chlamydospores. Due to morphological challenges, real-time PCR identified the species as Epidermophyton floccosum. The patient was treated with amoxicillin/clavulanic acid and topical terbinafine ointment.
